evidence.summary: Suggest NITRD for subject-matter expert review. Application 10213736 (FY2021), Advanced Computing/Computational Core at Stanford University, supports computer storage, high-performance computing, system administration, high-speed network access, and programming services for computational modeling and analysis in vision research. These computing infrastructure and software activities support the parent suggestion. The parent classifier returned NITRD with calibrated probability 0.99967 (decision threshold 0.3893682055460409). The public award record already includes the NITRD spending category. This is a review suggestion, not an official classification.

evidence_claim_check.claim: The public award record already includes the NITRD spending category.
evidence_claim_check.true: YES. In the snapshot (users.conroyri.nitrd_hackathon_v1_exporter_projects), 10213736 (FY2021, P30EY026877) has nih_spending_cats 'Bioengineering;Data Science;Eye Disease and Disorders of Vision;Networking and Information Technology R&D (NITRD);Neurosciences'. That includes the RCDC parent category (RePORTER id 329), stored by name. FY2021 is a build year, so this is not a reserved-year label read.
evidence_claim_check.grounded: YES. Call 1 of this run was outputs_get_project_detail {"appl_id": 10213736} (tool-call list below). That tool returns spending_categories and is_nitrd (src/nih_grants_outputs/tools/get_project_detail.py; identical at the deployed 95e5dea and d7bad89). For 10213736 they are the category list above, which includes NITRD, and is_nitrd true. The sentence restates that result. The other calls cannot be its source: classifier_classify_parent returns no category field (checked in code), and portal_get_review_history had no sandbox requests to return (0/0/0 after the row-10 cleanup).
